findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:10 — totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one too high whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 users, limit 50 → shows 3 pages instead of 2); as a result showingLast is never true on the real last page, the next control stays enabled, and users can navigate to an empty page. Should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — {{#unless automatic}} is evaluated in the item view's context, which is the member (a Discourse.User), not the group; automatic is always undefined there, so the remove link is rendered even for automatic groups where removal is prohibited, the guard never hides anything, and clicking the link always fails with a 422.

[Medium/api] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:33 (update, also create) — breaking change to the admin API contract: params are now read from the top level instead of the previous nested group: {...} payload, and the PATCH incremental-membership path was removed; existing API clients sending the old payload get a silent no-op (update returns success_json without applying any change), and since group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" is assigned unconditionally, an old-format request actually forces visible to false.

[Medium/api] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20 (members) — the public GET /groups/:name/members response changed from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no compatibility shim or versioning; any existing consumer of this endpoint (plugins, mobile clients, scripts) will break on the new shape.

[Medium/data] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:61 (add_members) — unknown usernames are silently skipped (if user = User.find_by_username(username)) and success_json is still returned even if zero members were actually added; the client gets no error or partial-success signal, so a typo'd username looks like a successful add (the UI just reloads with the member missing).

[Low/performance] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit and offset are taken directly from params with no maximum cap or validation on this public endpoint; a request with limit=100000 dumps the group's entire membership in one query, and negative values are passed through to the database unvalidated.

[Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:~90 — the "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members; it only passes because controller specs bypass routing, and it misdocuments the endpoint's HTTP verb (the passing "is able to remove a member" test correctly uses :delete).

[Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb — the rewritten GroupsController#members (pagination, meta payload, ordering, new default limit of 50) has no specs added or updated anywhere in this PR; the changed public behavior is untested.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:55 (addMembers) — the usernames input is never cleared after a successful add (acknowledged by the in-code TODO), and the promise returned by model.addMembers() is discarded, so a failed request (e.g., 422) gives the user no feedback at all.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — {{#unless automatic}} is evaluated in the item view's context, which is the member (a Discourse.User), not the group; automatic is always undefined there, so the remove link is rendered even for automatic groups where removal is prohibited, the guard never hides anything, and clicking the link always fails with a 422.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group_member.hbs`, the conditional `{{#unless automatic}}` is inside the per-member item view rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. The item template’s active context is the iterated `member` (a `Discourse.User`), and the diff does not show `automatic` being passed/bound into the `group-member` view. Thus `automatic` will be undefined/falsey in that context, making `{{#unless automatic}}` always true and rendering the remove link even for automatic groups. Server-side `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` explicitly blocks automatic groups with a 422, so the UI guard is broken as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:33 (update, also create) — breaking change to the admin API contract: params are now read from the top level instead of the previous nested group: {...} payload, and the PATCH incremental-membership path was removed; existing API clients sending the old payload get a silent no-op (update returns success_json without applying any change), and since group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" is assigned unconditionally, an old-format request actually forces visible to false.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real breaking/behavioral regression in `Admin::GroupsController`: `create` now reads `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` instead of the former nested `params[:group][:...]` (old code removed), and `update` now reads top-level params and removes the PATCH incremental membership path (`update_patch` deleted; `update` no longer branches on `request.patch?`). Critically, `update` assigns `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally (no presence check), so any update request that omits a top-level `visible` (including old-format clients sending `group: { visible: ... }`, or new clients updating only `alias_level`) will set `visible` to `false` and still return `success_json` if the save succeeds. That’s a verifiable incorrect behavior introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20 (members) — the public GET /groups/:name/members response changed from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no compatibility shim or versioning; any existing consumer of this endpoint (plugins, mobile clients, scripts) will break on the new shape.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupsController#members` changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (object with `members` + `meta`). There is no compatibility shim (e.g., keeping the old array shape, alternate endpoint, or versioning) shown in the diff, so any external consumer expecting an array would indeed break. This is an API compatibility concern rather than an internal correctness defect, since the PR also updates the JS client (`findMembers` now reads `result.members`/`result.meta`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:61 (add_members) — unknown usernames are silently skipped (if user = User.find_by_username(username)) and success_json is still returned even if zero members were actually added; the client gets no error or partial-success signal, so a typo'd username looks like a successful add (the UI just reloads with the member missing).

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each is conditionally added only if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; otherwise it is skipped. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if no users were found/added. This can make a typo look like a successful add with no explicit error/partial-success feedback. However, the diff also shows prior behavior intentionally “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” (that spec was removed along with the old PATCH-based membership update), so this is more a product/API feedback concern than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit and offset are taken directly from params with no maximum cap or validation on this public endpoint; a request with limit=100000 dumps the group's entire membership in one query, and negative values are passed through to the database unvalidated.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then applies them directly to `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or validation. This allows arbitrarily large `limit` values (potentially dumping/serializing huge membership lists) and allows negative offsets/limits (e.g. `-1`) to flow into the DB call, which can cause errors or unintended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb — the rewritten GroupsController#members (pagination, meta payload, ordering, new default limit of 50) has no specs added or updated anywhere in this PR; the changed public behavior is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially changes `GroupsController#members` behavior (now always paginates with default `limit` 50, accepts `offset`, orders by `username_lower`, and returns a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` in `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`). In the PR diff, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified/added to; there are no changes to (or additions of) any `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` or other specs covering `GroupsController#members`. So the changed public API behavior is left untested in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:55 (addMembers) — the usernames input is never cleared after a successful add (acknowledged by the in-code TODO), and the promise returned by model.addMembers() is discarded, so a failed request (e.g., 422) gives the user no feedback at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never resets `this.get("usernames")` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`. It also does not `return` the promise from `model.addMembers`, so the controller/action has no way to attach success/failure handling. However, the claim that a failed request gives the user “no feedback at all” is not fully verifiable from the diff alone because any global `Discourse.ajax` error handling is outside the shown changes; what is verifiable is the missing clear/reset and missing promise chaining/handling, which is a UX/completeness concern rather than a definite functional break.
